perOption.label: (A)
perOption.reason: 'where we are headed': 'be headed (+direction)' is the standard predicative past-participle idiom meaning 'be moving toward'; the fronted locative wh-word 'where' supplies the directional complement. NP + be + headed is fully grammatical ('heading' is an alternative, not a requirement).

perOption.label: (B)
perOption.reason: Parallel coordination after 'have to': 'have to [adjust to a postponement] or [create a whole new set of circumstances]' — two bare-infinitive VPs sharing the modal. 'create' properly takes the NP object. The verbal parse is available and semantically coherent (accommodate a delay or build new plans), so no parallelism violation.

perOption.label: (C)
perOption.reason: 'This is what happens when...': fused (free) relative 'what' with no antecedent, functioning as complement of 'is' and subject of 'happens'. 'that' would be impossible here for lack of an antecedent noun; 'what' is exactly what the structure requires.

perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'end up' obligatorily selects a gerund complement: 'end up spending' is the required form (*'end up to spend' is ungrammatical). 'spending' takes 'a few relaxing hours' as its object correctly.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: Clause-initial negative adverbial 'not only' inside the that-clause triggers obligatory subject-auxiliary inversion with a finite verb: 'not only ARE curveballs the universe's way..., but they are also...'. The correlative 'but they are also' proves a finite parallel clause is required. Gerund 'being' leaves the first conjunct with no finite verb and no legal word order; no rescue parse (absolute construction, gerund subject) is available since 'Remember that' demands a finite clause. Must be 'are'.

note: Uniquely determined error at (E): fronted 'not only' requires finite subject-auxiliary inversion ('not only are curveballs...'), which 'being' cannot satisfy. All other underlines verified correct under their governing rules (be headed idiom; modal-sharing VP coordination; free relative 'what'; end up + gerund). Alternative parses that might legitimize 'being' were actively searched and formally excluded.
